source_caption:
One of those movies that hits a lot harder than you expect.

Keanu Reeves plays Conor O’Neill, a gambler who agrees to coach a Little League team in Chicago. What starts as a way to make some money slowly becomes something much more meaningful, as the kids change his life just as much as he changes theirs.

The young cast is a huge part of why the movie works, especially DeWayne Warren as G-Baby. He brings so much personality and warmth to the character that even his smallest moments stay with you.

According to behind-the-scenes commentary, the scene where G-Baby explains why the pitcher needs “Big Poppa” was originally shorter and less emotional. The interaction was expanded during filming to bring out G-Baby’s sweet, insightful personality, and it became one of the film’s most memorable moments.

Hardball isn’t a perfect movie. Critics found it formulaic, but even they acknowledged its emotional moments and strong young cast.

Have you seen Hardball?

source_details.synopsis: Hardball is a 2001 American sports comedy-drama film co-produced and directed by Brian Robbins and starring Keanu Reeves in the main role, Diane Lane and D. B. Sweeney. The screenplay by John Gatins is based on the book Hardball: A Season in the Projects by Daniel Coyle. The original music score is composed by Mark Isham. The film was released by Paramount Pictures on September 14, 2001, topping the box office the weekend after the September 11 attacks by grossing $44.1 million against a $32 million budget.
